**Orglet 0.2.9** for Windows.

If you run 0.2.4 or later from Setup, this update arrives by itself and is used the next time you start Orglet.

### See how much of your plan is left

Settings → Local harnesses now shows who each Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent account is signed in as, and on which plan. For Claude Code and Codex you also get how much of each allowance is used and when it resets: the current session, the week, and a week limited to one model. The account picker shows this for every account, so you can tell which one still has room. Cursor Agent does not report usage, so its row shows the account and plan only.

For Claude Code, Orglet sends the CLI's own sign-in token to Anthropic's usage endpoint and nowhere else. It never renews or changes that token. If it has expired, open Claude Code once and choose Rescan.

### Switch accounts when one runs out

When a reply stops because the account ran out of plan usage, the bar above the message box offers another account that still has room, like "Codex ran out · Use Work · 70% left". One click switches to it and tries the reply again. If no other account has room, it tells you when yours resets.

### Fixes

- The login command a harness row copies now works in your own terminal. It used to point at a Claude desktop folder that only apps inside Claude could see. It now names your own install when you have one.
- A signed-out Cursor Agent shows as signed out instead of a sign-in error.

### Before you install

The installer is still not signed. Windows may say it protected your PC. If you downloaded Setup from this page, choose **More info → Run anyway**.

Orglet is open source under AGPL-3.0. This release ships for Windows only. Release checklist: [windows-release-gates.md](https://github.com/codepawl/orglet/blob/main/docs/windows-release-gates.md).
